Defines the ARN template. The provided string contains URI-template
style label placeholders that contain the name of one of the identifiers
defined in the `identifiers` property of the resource. These labels can
be substituted at runtime with the actual identifiers of the resource.
Every identifier name of the resource MUST have corresponding label of
the same name. Note that percent-encoding **is not** performed on these
placeholder values; they are to be replaced literally. For relative ARN
templates that have not set `absolute` to `true`, the template string
contains only the resource part of the ARN (for example,
`foo/{MyResourceId}`). Relative ARNs MUST NOT start with "/".

Set to true to indicate that the ARN template contains a fully-formed
ARN that does not need to be merged with the service. This type of ARN
MUST be used when the identifier of a resource is an ARN or is based on
the ARN identifier of a parent resource.

Set to true to specify that the ARN does not contain a region. If not
set, or if set to false, the resolved ARN will contain a placeholder
for the region. This can only be set to true if `absolute` is not set
or is false.

Set to true to specify that the ARN does not contain an account ID. If
not set, or if set to false, the resolved ARN will contain a placeholder
for the customer account ID. This can only be set to true if absolute
is not set or is false.

Defines which character is used to delimit sections of the resource
segment of an ARN. This can only be set if absolute is set to true.

Set to true to indicate that an ARN may be reused for different

The `sdkId` property is a required string value that specifies the AWS
SDK service ID (e.g., "API Gateway"). This value is used for generating
client names in SDKs and for linking between services.

The `arnNamespace` property is a string value that defines the ARN service
namespace of the service (e.g., "apigateway"). This value is used in
ARNs assigned to resources in the service. If not set, this value
defaults to the lowercase name of the service shape.

The `cloudFormationName` property is a string value that specifies the
AWS CloudFormation service name (e.g., `ApiGateway`). When not set,
this value defaults to the name of the service shape. This value is
part of the CloudFormation resource type name that is automatically
assigned to resources in the service (e.g., `AWS::<NAME>::resourceName`).

The `cloudTrailEventSource` property is a string value that defines the
AWS customer-facing eventSource property contained in CloudTrail event
records emitted by the service. If not specified, this value defaults
to the `arnNamespace` plus `.amazonaws.com`.

The `docId` property is a string value that defines the identifier
used to implement linking between service and SDK documentation for
AWS services. If not specified, this value defaults to the `sdkId` in
lower case plus the service `version` property, separated by dashes.

The `endpointPrefix` property is a string value that identifies which
endpoint in a given region should be used to connect to the service.
For example, most services in the AWS standard partition have endpoints
which follow the format: `{endpointPrefix}.{region}.amazonaws.com`. A
service with the endpoint prefix example in the region us-west-2 might
have the endpoint example.us-west-2.amazonaws.com.

This value is not unique across services and is subject to change.
Therefore, it MUST NOT be used for client naming or for any other
purpose that requires a static, unique identifier. sdkId should be used
for those purposes. Additionally, this value can be used to attempt to
resolve endpoints.

The `cloudWatchNamespace` property is a string value that defines the
AWS customer-facing namespace of most metrics emitted by the service.

An AWS service is defined using the `aws.api#service` trait. This trait
provides information about the service like the name used to generate AWS
SDK client classes and the namespace used in ARNs.

The `disableDefaultOperations` property is a boolean value that specifies
if the service does not have the standard tag operations supporting all
resources on the service. Default value is `false`

The signature version 4 service signing name to use in the credential
scope when signing requests. This value SHOULD match the `arnNamespace`
property of the `aws.api#service` trait if present and the `name`
property of the `aws.api#sigv4a` trait if present.

[Signature Version 4](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html)
is the process to add authentication information to AWS requests sent by HTTP. For
security, most requests to AWS must be signed with an access key, which consists
of an access key ID and secret access key. These two keys are commonly referred to
as your security credentials.

Signature Version 4 Asymmetric (SigV4A), an extension of Signature Version 4 (SigV4), is the
process to add authentication information to AWS requests sent by HTTP. SigV4A is nearly
identical to SigV4, but also uses public-private keys and asymmetric cryptographic signatures
for every request. Most notably, SigV4A supports signatures for multi-region API requests.

`requestAlgorithmMember` was removed, so newly generated clients will no longer be able to pick the request checksum algorithms The service MUST continue to support old clients by supporting `requestAlgorithmMember`.

smithy.test#eventStreamTests.documentation:
A duplex stream carries both initial messages: the input members
go out in an initial-request event and the output members come
back in an initial-response event, each ahead of their own
stream's events. Accept and Content-Type are both the event stream
media type because both directions stream.

EventStreamErrorOutput has no members besides the event stream, so
there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. A modeled error event
uses :message-type "exception" and names the union member in
:exception-type, and resolves to the modeled error shape rather than
a generic failure.

EventStreamErrorOutput has no members besides the event stream, so
there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. An error event arriving
after successfully delivered events still resolves to the modeled
error shape, so the events preceding it must not mask it.

EventStreamErrorOutput has no members besides the event stream, so
there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. Clients must handle a
structured but unmodeled error, which uses :message-type "error"
with the code and message carried entirely in headers and no
payload. No specification fixes the value of either :error-code or
:error-message, so only their presence is asserted.

EventStreamErrorOutput has no members besides the event stream, so
there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. A modeled error is sent
as an event with :message-type "exception" naming the union member
in :exception-type, with the error shape serialized as the CBOR
payload.

EventStreamErrorOutput has no members besides the event stream, so
there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. A modeled error raised
after events have already been sent is still sent as an exception
event, following the events that preceded it.

Non-stream input members are sent ahead of the stream. Under
rpcv2Cbor the operation's @httpHeader bindings are ignored, so
every non-stream input member travels in the CBOR payload of an
initial-request event rather than in HTTP headers.

Non-stream output members are delivered ahead of the stream. Under
rpcv2Cbor the operation's @httpHeader bindings are ignored, so
every non-stream output member travels in the CBOR payload of an
initial-response event rather than in HTTP response headers. This
output has non-stream members and values are provided for them, so
the initial-response event must be sent and the question the file
header leaves open does not arise here.

EventStreamRequestInput has no members besides the event stream, so
no initial request is modeled and there are no non-stream members to
serialize. This case pins the behavior of sending an initial-request
event anyway, ahead of the stream's events, carrying the
serialization of that empty set of members -- an empty CBOR map,
written as the canonical definite-length 0xa0 -- plus an
application/cbor :content-type. The streaming specification states
that when an initial request is not modeled a client MUST NOT send
one and a server MUST NOT expect one, and that a client or server
MUST NOT fail when an initial message containing only optional
members is not received. This case therefore asserts behavior the
specification forbids a client to produce, and it does NOT establish
conformance: a client that correctly omits the event fails it, and a
client that passes it has not been shown to conform. Serializes a
single struct-payload event onto a request stream as CBOR. An event
streaming request sets Content-Type to the event stream media type,
must not set a Content-Length, and must not name the operation in
either target header.

EventStreamRequestInput has no members besides the event stream, so
no initial request is modeled and there are no non-stream members to
serialize. This case pins the behavior of sending an initial-request
event anyway, ahead of the stream's events, carrying the
serialization of that empty set of members -- an empty CBOR map,
written as the canonical definite-length 0xa0 -- plus an
application/cbor :content-type. The streaming specification states
that when an initial request is not modeled a client MUST NOT send
one and a server MUST NOT expect one, and that a client or server
MUST NOT fail when an initial message containing only optional
members is not received. This case therefore asserts behavior the
specification forbids a client to produce, and it does NOT establish
conformance: a client that correctly omits the event fails it, and a
client that passes it has not been shown to conform. Serializes a
sequence of events onto a request stream, closing with an
empty-structure event that carries no payload.

EventStreamResponseOutput has no members besides the event stream,
so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. Deserializes an event
whose implicit payload carries every scalar type: the blob is a raw
CBOR byte string rather than base64, the timestamp is tag 1 epoch
seconds, the enum is its string value and the intEnum is an integer.

EventStreamResponseOutput has no members besides the event stream,
so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. Deserializes an event
whose payload carries lists of scalars as CBOR arrays.

EventStreamResponseOutput has no members besides the event stream,
so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. Deserializes an event
whose payload carries maps of scalars as CBOR maps with text string
keys.

EventStreamResponseOutput has no members besides the event stream,
so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. Deserializes an event
whose payload nests a structure, which is a CBOR map keyed by member
name like any other.

EventStreamResponseOutput has no members besides the event stream,
so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. Deserializes an event
whose payload nests a union, serialized as a CBOR map with exactly
one member set.

EventStreamResponseOutput has no members besides the event stream,
so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case pins the
reading under which an initial-response event is sent anyway and its
payload is the serialization of that empty set of members, an empty
CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor :content-type. The competing
reading, under which no initial response exists to be sent, is
unresolved against it; see the file header. Dispatches a sequence of
events to the correct union variants. The heartbeat event models an
empty structure, so it carries no payload.

EventStreamResponseBlobPayloadOutput has no members besides the
event stream, so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This
case pins the reading under which an initial-response event is sent
anyway and its payload is the serialization of that empty set of
members, an empty CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor
:content-type. The competing reading, under which no initial
response exists to be sent, is unresolved against it; see the file
header. A blob @eventPayload is written as the raw message payload,
neither CBOR nor base64, and takes the application/octet-stream
content type. The modeled @eventHeader member is carried as a
message header and does not appear in the payload.

EventStreamResponseHeadersOutput has no members besides the event
stream, so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This case
pins the reading under which an initial-response event is sent
anyway and its payload is the serialization of that empty set of
members, an empty CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor
:content-type. The competing reading, under which no initial
response exists to be sent, is unresolved against it; see the file
header. Each @eventHeader member is carried as a typed event stream
message header rather than in the payload, so the event stream
framing fixes their encoding and this protocol does not. A string
@eventPayload is written as raw text and takes the text/plain
content type.

EventStreamResponseStructPayloadOutput has no members besides the
event stream, so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This
case pins the reading under which an initial-response event is sent
anyway and its payload is the serialization of that empty set of
members, an empty CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor
:content-type. The competing reading, under which no initial
response exists to be sent, is unresolved against it; see the file
header. A structure @eventPayload is written as the CBOR message
payload and takes the application/cbor content type. The modeled
@eventHeader member is carried as a message header and does not
appear in the payload.

EventStreamResponseUnionPayloadOutput has no members besides the
event stream, so there are no non-stream members to serialize. This
case pins the reading under which an initial-response event is sent
anyway and its payload is the serialization of that empty set of
members, an empty CBOR map, carrying an application/cbor
:content-type. The competing reading, under which no initial
response exists to be sent, is unresolved against it; see the file
header. A union @eventPayload is written as the CBOR message payload
and takes the application/cbor content type. The modeled
@eventHeader member is carried as a message header and does not
appear in the payload.

The type of event - request or response.

The parameters used to generate the event.

If set, these parameters MUST be compatible with a modeled event.

If not set, this event represents an unmodeled event.

A map of expected headers.

Headers that are not listed in this map are ignored unless they are
explicitly forbidden through `forbidHeaders`.

A list of header field names that must not appear in the serialized
event.

A list of header field names that must appear in the serialized
event, but no assertion is made on the value.

Headers listed in `headers` do not need to appear in this list.

The expected event body.

If no request body is defined, then no assertions are made about
the body of the event.

The media type of the `body`.

This is used to help test runners to parse and validate the expected
data against generated data.

An optional binary representation of the entire event.

This is used to test deserialization. If set, implementations SHOULD
use this value to represent the binary value of received events rather
than constructing that binary value from the other properties of the
event.

This value SHOULD NOT be used to make assertions about serialized
events as such assertions likely would not be reliable. They would
suffer from the same problems of making body assertions without a
bodyMediaType where nonspecified ordering and optional whitespace
can cause semantically equivalent values to have different bytes. This
is made worse by headers having no defined order, and is likely made
even worse by common event framing features such as checksums.

variables, configuration files on disk, or other means to influence

with that shape's definition.

Byte headers MUST be written in the model as base64-encoded
strings, e.g. `Zm9v` represents utf8 `foo`.

A typed event header value. This is needed to disambiguate
types that the Smithy Node would otherwise not be able to.

A map of event headers. The value is a union to indicate type,
but it MUST be serialized / deserialized without any sort of
wrapping from the union.

The union value type is needed to disambiguate types that the
Smithy Node would otherwise not be able to. This can't be a
simple map like for HTTP headers because HTTP headers only have
one value type, and the Smithy IDL isn't able to distinguish
between types like byte/short without some additional layer.
